summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and Hodgkin’s lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant presented with acute abdominal pain and markedly increased watery ostomy output. She was febrile on admission with CT findings of small bowel wall thickening suggestive of enteritis. Infectious workup was negative for C. difficile, bacterial pathogens, parasites, and CMV, with stool viral culture also negative. Symptoms improved with supportive care, including IV fluids and electrolyte repletion. She was discharged home after clinical improvement on a short course of oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, with instructions to complete potassium supplementation and follow up with her transplant and oncology teams.
